bull_bear.body: Interim dividend approved: 25% of face value (Rs. 0.50/share), total outflow ~Rs. 1,691 mn; M&A focused on Africa (Twizza closed, Crickley pending) to broaden portfolio and utilize existing capacity; Disciplined working capital management.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension impacting crude/oil prices (transportation & packaging costs); Unseasonal weather (rains) disrupting summer sales; Aluminum can shortage constraining energy drink volumes; Intense competition (Campa, Coke) leading to potential price wars; Currency fluctuation in African markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and bullish on long-term structural growth (double-digit for 5-10 years); Pragmatic on near-term inflation (hedged, but monitoring); Aggressive on distribution expansion and market share gains; Emphasizes operational efficiency and scale advantages over competitors.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management claims 6-month raw material inventory in international markets (vs industry norm of much less), providing a significant competitive cost advantage during inflation; Shift from greenfield capex to M&A in Africa indicates a strategy to instantly acquire capacity and route-to-market rather than build; Realization decline in India (-1.5%) is improving sequentially (-4% in prior quarter) due to premiumization (dairy, new launches) and discount cuts, despite pack upsizing.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "In accordance with our dividend policy, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of 25% of face value, i.e., Rs. 0.50 per share, resulting in a total cash outflow of approximately ~Rs. 1,691 million."
- "VBL India continued to remain Net debt free with a free cash of ~ Rs.14,941 million, however, at the consolidated level net debt stood at ~ Rs. 3,730 million as on June 30, 2026, on account of acquisition of Twizza in South Africa."
- "Company's long-term rating for bank loan facilities from CRISIL (an S&P Global Company) is reaffirmed as CRISIL AAA/Stable."
- The performance-highlights chart shows Net D/E of 0.0 for the three most recent periods (2024, 2025, H1 2026) versus 0.8/0.7/0.7/0.7 in the earlier years shown, alongside "NET WORTH CAGR (2020-25) – 40.6%".
- Capital deployment is split between organic capex (~Rs. 9,500 million net capitalized in H1 CY2026) and inorganic territory/business acquisitions (Twizza Rs. 11,314 million; DFIKL Kenya USD 32 million).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: CSD: 73.6% of volumes; NCB: 7.5%; Water: 18.9%; Low/No-sugar mix: ~63% of total volume; India Volume: +14.4%; International Volume: +21.4% (broad-based across Africa, not just SA); Dairy segment growing 60-70%; Energy drinks (Sting, Ad-Rush) seeing strong demand, constrained by can shortage.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Key player in the global beverage industry and the second largest franchisee of PepsiCo in the world (outside US) with franchise operations spanning across 10 countries and with distribution rights in additional 4 countries."
- "Symbiotic Relationship with PepsiCo": VBL owns Demand Delivery (production facilities, sales & distribution/GTM & logistics, in-outlet visi-coolers, BTL consumer push) while PepsiCo owns Demand Creation (trademarks, concentrate formulation, product/packaging R&D, ATL brand development).
- "34+ Years of Association (agreement in India valid till April, 2049)" and "90%+ of PepsiCo India Sales Volume".
- Franchise footprint: "VBL has been granted franchises for various PepsiCo products across 26 States and 6 Union Territories in India", plus Nepal, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Lesotho, Eswatini & DRC, with distribution rights for Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique and Madagascar.
- "India is the largest market and contributed ~67% of revenues from operations (net) in Fiscal 2025."
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [PepsiCo EBA] "VBL and PepsiCo Inc. and its affiliates have entered into a revised Exclusive bottling appointment and trademark license agreement for India ('EBA') on May 21, 2026", with "(i) extension of the EBA term to April 30, 2049 (from April 30, 2039), and (ii) removal of the earlier restriction requiring VBL to operate solely as an SPV for PepsiCo's business, providing greater operational flexibility to explore, expand and avail benefits of scale and synergies."
- [Asahi/CALPIS] "On 18 June 2026, VBL has entered into a business alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce and commercialize the CALPIS brand in India through a franchise arrangement"; CALPIS is "Japan's iconic fermented milk-based beverage brand with a legacy of over 100 years".
- [Kenya acquisition] "On 06 July 2026, VBL Industries (Kenya) Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of VBL has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire the business in DFIKL, a promoter group company, for a purchase consideration of USD 32 million (~INR 3,050 million, 1 USD = 95.30 INR) based upon the valuation of net assets from an independent third-party valuer."
- [Kenya acquisition] "DFIKL has net revenue of over Rs. 3,000 million for value added dairy, juices, packaged drinking water, etc. for the financial year ended March 2026. DFIKL also has an existing GTM infrastructure in place", and the deal "will provide us with the ready GTM in Kenya for expansion into carbonated soft drinks and energy drinks".
- [Snacks] Beyond beverages, VBL does "Manufacturing & Distribution of PepsiCo's snack foods in Morocco and Zimbabwe and distribution in Zambia; Co-manufacturing of Kurkure Puffcorn in India", and "Manufacturing & Distribution of own brands is restricted in select territories".

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
